question: What phenotype would you expect in an individual in whom an immunodeficiency caused by a mutation homozygous for the CD3ε chain that prevents the expression of this molecular complex has been described ?:

options.opa: Inability to perform an immune response in any situation.
options.opb: Inability to perform cellular responses to viruses and intracellular bacteria, but with a normal humoral response.
options.opc: It will only be able to perform an innate and adaptive humoral response Tindependiente.
options.opd: Problems to perform responses to extracellular bacteria and fungi.

analysis: The CD3ε chain is a critical component of the T-cell receptor (TCR) complex, which is essential for T-cell activation and function. A mutation that prevents the expression of this chain would lead to a severe impairment in T-cell development and function, resulting in a profound immunodeficiency. This would manifest as an inability to mount any adaptive immune response, including both cellular (T-cell mediated) and humoral (B-cell mediated) responses. Therefore, the most appropriate phenotype expected in this scenario is the inability to perform an immune response in any situation.
